flutter.themeMode: ThemeMode.system by default; Settings can pin light or dark (theme_controller.dart)
flutter.font: Inter static TTFs 400/500/600/700 bundled in mobile/assets/fonts/inter with OFL LICENSE.txt; family 'Inter' in pubspec.yaml; FontFeature.tabularFigures on every style; letterSpacing = em * fontSize
flutter.palette: CanaryPalette ThemeExtension (context.palette): ground, panel, raised, well, hairline, hairlineStrong, text, textSecondary, muted, accent, accentText, safeText, attentionText, alarmText, wordmarkDot; light and darkPalette

paletteHelpers.ink(solid): the theme's -text step for a state solid
paletteHelpers.tint(solid, alpha=22): solid alpha-blended over panel; +6 alpha in dark

narrative.overview: A building-safety operations console for a dispatcher under time pressure, with a manager and a technician behind them. Cool near-neutral surfaces, 1px hairlines, one blue accent, precise Inter type with tabular numerals. Dark is the default; light is a full second theme on the same token names. Colour means state and nothing else; with every other surface held neutral, an alarm is the loudest thing on any screen. The shell reports building state on every page through the incident count on the Dispatch destination. The resident app (mobile/, Flutter) runs on these tokens and rules; it is a phone adaptation of the Quiet Console, not a second world. Home is one status block, then the rooms as plain labelled cards, inside three bottom tabs (Home, Household, Settings). Under alarm the whole phone takes the incident-banner language full-screen. Unlike the dashboard, the phone follows the device's light / dark setting by default (Settings can pin light or dark); both themes are complete on the same names.
keyCharacteristics: Three surface steps (ground, panel, raised) separated by 1px hairlines, not shadows.
State colour has three steps each: solid, text, soft tint, re-tuned per theme.
Long repeated lists collapse into compact state cells and matrices with the full sentence on tooltip and accessible name.
Evacuation is the one place the system gets loud: deep red, a slim black-and-amber tape strip, ISO pictograms.

rules.name: The State-Only Colour Rule
rules.body: Green, amber and red mean state. They never decorate, never mark a category, never fill a series.

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: Blue means "you can act on this" or "this is selected". Motion cells use blue as selection-like info, never as a hazard.

rules.name: The Neutral Demo Rule
rules.body: The Demo badge is a neutral outlined pill. Demo is not a hazard state.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Labels are sentence case at 12px muted. No uppercase, no tracked-out eyebrows or kickers.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Numbers are tabular everywhere; never swap in a proportional face for a figure.

rules.name: The Flat Surface Rule
rules.body: Cards, tiles and cells never carry a shadow at rest. Only overlays do.

rules.name: The No-Glow Rule
rules.body: No glows, no coloured side stripes. A selected item uses the accent border plus a 1px ring.

rules.name: The Shape-And-Colour Mark Rule
rules.body: On the phone every state mark is a shape as well as a colour: a dot for normal, a rounded square for attention, a triangle for alarm, evacuation and danger, a 1.6px ring for unknown or offline. The status block, room tiles and scope chips all use it.

rules.name: The Needs-A-Look Tint Rule
rules.body: Room tiles and reading cells stay on Panel or Well while normal. Only attention and danger take the soft tint, the state border and state-coloured text.

rules.name: The Bundled Face Rule
rules.body: The phone never falls back to the platform face: every style names Inter, and the four weights ship in the app.

dos: Do use green, amber and red only for state, always as a dot or fill plus text, with a soft tint behind it.
Do use the -text step of a colour for text and the solid step for dots, fills and borders.
Do keep blue for action and selection, and one primary button per panel.
Do build both themes from the same token names; add a light value whenever a dark one is added.
Do compact long repeated lists into state cells or matrices, keeping the full sentence as tooltip and accessible name.
Do separate chart series by dash pattern as well as by colour, and keep series to the five data colours.
Do honour prefers-reduced-motion for every pulse.
Do pair every state colour on the phone with its shape mark: dot, square, triangle, ring.
Do keep room tiles and reading cells neutral while normal; tint only what needs a look.
Do follow the phone's light / dark setting by default, and keep both CanaryPalette themes complete.
Do send state text through palette.ink() and tints through palette.tint(), never a raw solid on Panel.
Do keep tap targets at 48px and let button pairs stack when their labels would not fit on one line.
donts: Don't use state colours to decorate or categorise.
Don't use blue or violet for hazard, or green / amber / red for series.
Don't add glows, coloured side stripes, or shadows at rest.
Don't add uppercase labels, eyebrows or kickers.
Don't treat Demo mode as a hazard state; keep its badge neutral and outlined.
Don't use the black-and-amber tape or deep red outside evacuation.
Don't introduce a fourth surface step or a radius beyond 4, 6, 8 and 12.
Don't let Material defaults back in on the phone: no seeded colour scheme, no surface tint, no resting elevation, no fully rounded buttons.
Don't use Deepened Safe Green outside the check-in button.
